author: thestreet.com
title: Is Dow 30,000 Again a Reality?
text:
Bring on the gains.
Dow 30,000 Believe it or not, we are only 24% away from Dow Jones Industrial Average 30,000. Thinking about hitting that large number by early 2019 is logical after seeing the benchmark index explode 669 points on Monday. After all, if investors could shrug off fears of a trade war, a chaotic White House, rising interest rates and unrest over how companies with market caps of nearly a trillion dollars are using our data why shouldn't the Dow reach 30,000? Factor in the profit tailwind that are tax cuts, and the elixir is there for a powerful rally. Think I am dumb? Feel free to yell at me on Twitter @BrianSozzi but just be sure to mention you read this on @TheStreet .
Your Daily Facebook Pound of Flesh What is the deal here with Facebook's ( FB ) Mark Zuckerberg? Zuck reportedly declined an invitation to face lawmakers in the U.K. to discuss the Cambridge Analytica situation, pointed out TheStreet's Martin Baccardax . This comes after a weekend full of lame apology ads in newspapers by Zuck. Is hiding and throwing cash at the PR crisis (and operational crisis) some form of new leadership style that's in vogue in Silicon Valley? Is this some kind of new Tony Robbins approach to leading during times of extreme duress? (I'm a big fan of Robbins -- Tone, come on back down to TheStreet ). But for real, the lack of leadership by Zuckerberg right now is bordering on disturbing. He has to lay it all on the line, once and for all. Take the public beating after testifying in the U.K. and U.S., get the worst case (or try to) baked into Facebook's stock. Go on the offensive. If Facebook's stock doesn't give back its early Tuesday gains off this news I would be surprised.
Hot Stats for Tuesday Share these on social media, use them for talking points at the coffee maker or post them in your blog with full credit to me -- your call. (1) S&P 500 earnings estimates for the first quarter have fallen for the third straight week, according to Yardeni Research. The S&P 500's first-quarter forecast was down to $36.13 last week from $36.20 a week earlier. Why you should care: Wall Street is working its contacts and sensing that sluggish first-quarter GDP growth could mean some unfortunate earnings surprises. Time to lighten up on those industrial stocks, bro. (2) The biggest overweight sectors in the market -- tech, industrials and materials -- lagged during the market rout last week while the largest underweight sectors outperformed. Why you should care: Traders are now long what I call garbage stocks , those companies with slow or no growth potential that catch client money during extreme points of stress in the market. Think packaged food companies and utilities. With the market poised to continue Monday's rally on Tuesday , the rotation back into high growth names such as Action Alerts Plus holdings Amazon ( AMZN ) and Apple ( AAPL ) could keep the momentum going for the rest of the week. (3) Action Alerts Plus holding Microsoft's stock the past year: up 43% vs. Apple's stock the past year: Up 0%. Why you should care: Microsoft's relative out-performance is no surprise. The company has morphed into an innovation machine under CEO Satya Nadella whereas Apple has had a few product flubs. Go figure.
